extracted.subtask_description: AP news dispatches reporting on Cold War–era political, military and diplomatic events (hearings, UN conferences, island conflicts), intended as front‑page news for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference scope: exchange of information only
rubrics_metrics.description: "the conference is for exchange of information only."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule (quoted): no proposals requiring adoption by voting shall be submitted or entertained; the conference is intended as an informational exchange rather than a decisionmaking body.

rubrics_metrics.name: No proposals requiring adoption by voting
rubrics_metrics.description: "NO PROPOSALS REQUIRING ADOPTION BY VOTING SHALL BE SUBMITTED OR ENTERTAINED BY THE CONFERENCE."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition on introducing items that would require voting or formal adoption — limits the conference to nonbinding technical/scientific exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings will be published
rubrics_metrics.description: "The committee also agreed that the conference proceedings will be published."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference materials and reports are to be made public in published proceedings, implying transparency and archival record of technical discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports to be presented from scientific and technical viewpoint only
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports will be "presented only from the scientific and technical points of view."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline to exclude political or propagandistic framing of submissions; presentations should focus on technical/scientific content and applications (e.g., reactor design, isotopes, waste disposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: President/chairmen empowered to curb irrelevant or political remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: The president "may call a speaker to [order] if remarks are not relevant" and the conference president was described as "empowered to rule out political discussion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting chairs have authority to enforce relevance and exclude political or propagandistic interventions to keep sessions technical and on-task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings/papers: oral presentation emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention that "papers should be presented orally" (rules specify which papers should be presented orally).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on oral presentation of papers in sessions (as opposed to solely written submissions), likely to prioritize live technical exchange and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural safeguards against propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules intended "to guard against the propaganda exchanges which have impeded so many postwar international conferences" (including forbidding political proposals, restricting viewpoints to technical/scientific, and giving chair control).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suite of procedural rules (no voting on proposals, technical-only reports, chair authority) explicitly designed to minimize political propaganda and keep focus on peaceful uses of atomic energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army/investigations must follow Supreme Court guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that "the Army must act in accordance with the Supreme Court's guidance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in context of investigations/administrative action (e.g., determining subversive conduct or personnel action): suggests that military procedures and disciplinary measures should conform to Supreme Court rulings and constitutional protections.
